verdict.rationale: Aider's own commands cover reproducing and verifying. `/run` executes code and can share the output with the LLM, and `/test` plus `--auto-test` run the test suite after edits. Root-cause narrowing rests only on `/ask` and the repo map, which are general codebase Q&A features, plus community reports of using Aider to understand codebases. missing for 10: a documented debugging or root-cause workflow (e.g. a debugger, tracing or bisect support), explicit docs on reproducing reported issues, and independent hands-on evidence of the fix-verify loop working in practice.

support.subject: As a developer, I can reproduce issues, narrow down root causes, and verify fixes

citations.quote: You can use the `/run` command in the chat to run your code and optionally share the output with aider.
You can configure aider to run your test suite after each time the AI edits your code using the --test-cmd <test-command> and --auto-test switch.
If there are test errors, aider expects the command to print them on stdout/stderr and return a non-zero exit code.
Ask questions about the code base without editing any files.
Aider can answer questions I can't search for via LSP, like 'what code would process the following URL' and similar.
